chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran and Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abd Allah ibn Maskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who cut off the head of a dead body, he said: The blood money is due, because its sanctity when dead is like its sanctity when alive.
ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for cutting off the head of a corpse?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing that the *diyah* (blood money) for severing a corpse's head is equivalent to that of a living person, grounded in the principle that bodily sanctity (*hurmat*) persists after death. This hadith is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for determining compensation in cases of *qatl al-janazah* (killing the dead), affirming that the physical integrity of the deceased retains legal value comparable to the living.
